name: Topic 35: Overhydration and low sodium (hyponatremia)
defaultTargetFormula: No new target. Use Topic 30 target_ml = base(sex: male 2500, female 2000, unknown 2500) + clamp((weight_kg - ref_weight) * 20, -400, 400) + min(workout_minutes * 8, 1000) + (hot_weather ? 500 : 0) + pregnancy/lactation adds; Topic 31 heat adds; clamp 1500-4500 ml; round to 50 ml. Overhydration guards (est.): level 1 soft warning if logged_ml in rolling 60 min > 750; level 2 if >= 1000 ml in 60 min or >= 1500 ml in 120 min; daily soft warning at the user's cap (max 4500 ml); daily hard stop above 5000 ml with doctor note and confirm tap; guards never raise the target. ICMR-NIN 2020 overhydration threshold Not found.

drinks.name: Plain water
drinks.notes: No sodium; large fast volumes can dilute blood sodium

drinks.name: WHO/UNICEF reduced-osmolarity ORS
drinks.notes: 75 mmol/L sodium (about 1724 mg per litre, calc.), 75 mmol/L glucose, 245 mOsm/L; for diarrhoea or vomiting only; made with the stated water volume

drinks.name: Sports or electrolyte drink
drinks.notes: About 18 mmol/L sodium (about 420 mg per litre, calc.), 6% carbohydrate (secondary); does not replace drinking to thirst

drinks.name: Chaas (salted)
drinks.notes: About 85-200 mg sodium per 100 ml (secondary, unverified); depends on salt added; counts toward Topic 18 sodium

drinks.name: Nimbu pani with a pinch of salt
drinks.notes: est.; about 200 mg sodium per 250 ml from the pinch of salt; sugar varies

drinks.name: Tender coconut water
drinks.notes: Low sodium (about 15-28 mg per 100 ml, sources differ), potassium-rich; not a sodium fix; Topic 19 caution

drinks.name: Tea or coffee
drinks.notes: First 4 cups per Topic 33; low sodium

drinks.name: Fruit juice or soft drink
drinks.notes: est.; product policy; sugar, little sodium

drinks.name: Alcohol or beer
drinks.notes: Not counted; beer potomania risk with low solute intake

drinksTable.notes: No sodium (tap and mineral water vary); the usual drink in overhydration; sodium diluted if drunk in large volumes quickly
75 mmol/L sodium (about 1,724 mg per litre, calc.; about 345 mg per 200 ml), 75 mmol/L glucose, 245 mOsm/L (Topic 34, WHO/UNICEF); not a daily drink; made with the stated water
45 mmol/L sodium (about 1,035 mg/L, calc.), 2.5% carbohydrate (Nutrients 2023); not WHO formula

About 18.3 mmol/L sodium (about 420 mg per litre, calc.), 3.3 mmol/L potassium, 6% carbohydrate (Bell and Spriet); Gatorade retail about 45-49 mg per 100 ml (Topic 32); sugar load; only partly replaces sweat sodium
Plain chaas about 85 mg sodium and 142 mg potassium per 100 ml (database, Topic 33); masala up to about 200 mg per 100 ml; a 200 ml glass about 170-400 mg sodium (est.); depends on salt added

drinksTable.drink: Nimbu pani with a pinch of salt
drinksTable.notes: About 200 mg sodium per 250 ml from the salt, 8-10 g sugar (est., calc., Topic 33); salt and sugar adjustable

Sodium about 6.6 mmol/L (about 150 mg per litre, 15 mg per 100 ml, calc.; Bell and Spriet) but IFCT 2017 gives 28 mg per 100 g; potassium about 50 mmol/L (about 215 mg per 100 g, IFCT); sources disagree, so it is a low-sodium drink and not a sodium fix (Topic 19 for potassium caution)
Low sodium (milk adds some); caffeine 30-120 mg per cup (Topic 33); large volumes of tea with little food is a "tea and toast" risk
High sugar; little sodium; heavy volumes contribute fluid without sodium
Beer potomania (low solute plus high volume); not counted

reminderRules.rule: Soft warning when logged water exceeds 750 ml in any rolling 60 minutes; pause reminders for 2 hours
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); Topic 32 ceiling; EAH consensus 2015 drink-to-thirst

reminderRules.rule: Strong warning when 1000 ml or more is logged in 60 minutes or 1500 ml or more in 2 hours; stop reminders for the day; show symptoms and 'call 112' red flags
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); kidney excretion about 0.8-1.0 L/h (Verbalis via Scientific American; secondary, unverified)

reminderRules.rule: Daily soft warning at the user's target cap (maximum 4500 ml) with 'No need to go beyond this'; hard stop with confirm tap and doctor note above 5000 ml
'I feel unwell' with confusion, severe headache, repeated vomiting, seizure or collapse shows 'Call 112, do not drink more water'
reminderRules.source: European hyponatraemia guideline 2014 symptom classes; WMS 2019 EAH guideline (via snippets, secondary)

reminderRules.rule: Doctor-flag users (heart, kidney or liver disease, SIADH, thiazide, SSRI, carbamazepine, MDMA, labour, fluid limit): remove target and reminders, ask for the doctor's ml limit and warn at 100% of it
reminderRules.source: Liamis review; NICE and UK NHS trust labour guidance; Topic 34 (secondary); requires_doctor_input

reminderRules.rule: Fasting (vrat) days: show 'sip to thirst' and a salted chaas or nimbu pani idea, no extra water reminders
No water reminders during or within 2 hours after a level 1 or 2 warning; exercise sessions over 1 hour show drink-to-thirst

warnings: General information, not medical advice. Low blood sodium (hyponatraemia, serum sodium below 135 mmol/L) can be an emergency.
Confusion, severe headache, repeated vomiting, seizure or collapse after heavy drinking: call 112 and do not give more water or fluid.
Healthy kidneys clear about 0.8-1.0 L of water per hour at best, less during long exercise (secondary, unverified): do not chug litres in an hour.
Drink to thirst during exercise; do not force fluid and do not use salt tablets or home saline without a doctor.
Heart, kidney or liver disease, SIADH, thiazide diuretics, SSRIs, carbamazepine, MDMA, pregnancy and labour, and infants: follow your doctor's or midwife's fluid advice (requires_doctor_input).
Very low salt and low protein diets with large volumes of tea or water can lower blood sodium; do not stop BP medicine or add extra water.
ORS is for diarrhoea or vomiting only and must be made with the stated water volume.
No ICMR-NIN 2020 overhydration limit found; 1000 ml/h and 5000 ml/day marks are FitPlate (est.); all other numbers are secondary, unverified.
